The page is complete. Let me verify the facts on the page against the fact sheet one final time.

Done. `landing/index.html` is a single self-contained file, ready to review by opening it in a browser.

**What I built**
- **Content** — every claim maps 1:1 to `FACTSHEET.md`: painter (Piet Mondrian, 1872–1944, Dutch), year (1930), medium (oil on canvas), collection (Kunsthaus Zurich), alternate title (Composition II…), movement (De Stijl, founded 1917 by van Doesburg and Mondrian), Neoplasticism principles, the picture's layout, why it matters (asymmetric primary-colour balance as a reference for graphic design and architecture), and a "Read more" CTA linking to the fact sheet's Wikipedia source. Nothing beyond the fact sheet is asserted — the only added text is rhetorical framing of listed facts.
- **Mondrian's visual language** — the hero contains a reproduction of the composition built as a pure CSS grid (large red square top-right, small blue square bottom-left, yellow rectangle bottom-right, thick black rules on white). Sections use black-gapped "rule" grids, primary-color chips and accent bars, Archivo Black uppercase type.
- **three.js** — a decorative, very subtle drifting black-line shader (loaded as a module from the exact allowed CDN URL) sits behind the page inside a `try/catch`; if the CDN or WebGL fails, the page is visually complete without it. Only external requests are Google Fonts and the pinned three.js URL. Responsive layout collapses to one column under 800px.

**Assumptions I made (brief left them open)**
- The CSS-grid reproduction stands in for the actual image (no image CDN is reachable), with an explicit caption and `aria-label` saying it's schematic.
- Red/blue/yellow hex values are Mondrian-ish approximations, not colorimetric claims.

**How I know it's right**: I re-grepped the finished file for every date, name, and institution and confirmed each matches the fact sheet exactly; the fact grid in the "The painting" section restates all six listed attributes verbatim. The HTML/CSS/JS is plain static code with no build step, and the three.js path is guarded so the only failure mode is a hidden canvas.
